Required setback distance at a height

Source: R/setbacks.R
setback_distance.Rd

Evaluates a setback rule at one or more heights. The engine calls this for every boundary at every storey; it is exported so rules can be checked and plotted on their own.

Usage

setback_distance(
  rule,
  height,
  storey = NA_integer_,
  bearing = NA_real_,
  vars = list(),
  slope_in = 0,
  base_height = height,
  measured = NULL
)

Arguments

rule

A setback from yard(), plane() and friends (or the same structure read from a rulebook file).

height

Height(s) above the datum (m) at which to evaluate.

storey

Storey number(s) for rules with from_storey; defaults to NA, which counts as satisfying any storey condition.

bearing

Bearing(s) of the boundary's outward normal (degrees clockwise from north), for planes whose angle depends on orientation.

vars

Other variables for formula values, see eval_rule_value().

slope_in

For planes on sloping ground: how fast the site's ground rises into the site from the boundary (metres per metre).

base_height

The building's own height above the site's ground, where height has been adjusted to the boundary's ground; a plane's max_setback_above is tested against it.

measured

For a yard with value_from: the measured distance (m) per height (NA where nothing was measured).

Value

Numeric vector of required distances (m), one per height.

Examples

p <- plane(angle_deg = 45, start_height = 2.5, boundaries = "side")
setback_distance(p, c(2, 3, 6, 9))
#> [1] 0.0 0.5 3.5 6.5
setback_distance(proportional_setback(0.4, "side", min = 3), c(3, 10, 20))
#> [1] 3 4 8
